findings.title: The sync-mode schema requires a literal property instead of an expiry field
findings.body: `[z.string().toString()]` evaluates to the literal key `"[object Object]"`; it does not define a wildcard numeric property. Consequently, refresh responses that contain the documented access token and an expiry field fail validation unless they also contain a numeric `"[object Object]"` field. With credential syncing enabled, token refreshes for providers using this parser therefore fail instead of accepting the sync endpoint's response.

findings.title: Stores the Zod safeParse wrapper as the Google credential key
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the result of `safeParse`, which is an object shaped like `{ success, data }`, but this caller assigns that entire result to `key` and persists it as the credential. The next Google auth attempt parses this wrapper as token credentials and cannot find the access/refresh token fields, breaking the connected calendar and its future refreshes.

findings.title: Refreshes Salesforce tokens but builds the connection with the old tokens
findings.body: After obtaining and persisting `accessTokenParsed.data`, the returned connection is initialized from `credentialKey.instance_url` and `credentialKey.access_token`, the stale values loaded before refresh. When the old access token has expired, Salesforce API calls use that expired token even though a fresh token was just obtained and stored, so the integration fails until another credential reload.

findings.title: Sends the credential ID as the synced user's ID
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens` uses its third argument as `calcomUserId` in the request sent to the self-hosted sync endpoint. This call passes `credentialId`, not `credential.userId`; credential IDs and user IDs are separate identifiers, so the remote app store looks up the wrong user and cannot refresh that user's token. Pass the owning user's ID from the credential instead.

findings.title: Sends the credential ID as the synced user's ID
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens` uses its third argument as `calcomUserId` in the request sent to the self-hosted sync endpoint. This call passes `credential.userId`, but the shown method's credential is available here; correction: this line actually passes the correct user ID. No issue.
